title: The whole system on one page
html:
Thirty findings, boiled down to what you actually do on draft night. Every rule links to its write-up — click through to see the data and how sure we are.

Before you pick

  • Bring a list and follow it. Sticking to credible rankings beats

    • drafting by feel by about ten points of season strength. Everything else on this page is a fight over the last one. Finding 03

  • Spend your prep on players, not draft tricks. Knowing who's good

    • beats clever pick order about 40 to 1. Finding 24

  • Use our board, with one caution. The projections out-rank the

    • draft market at QB, WR and TE — at RB, follow the market. Finding 25

Rounds 1–3: running backs

  • Open RB-RB-RB. In 1,440 simulated seasons of our league it won

    • the title 20% of the time — two and a half times the fair share. Finding 01

  • The reason: RBs run out first. Running back value falls off

    • almost twice as fast as receiver value, and the waiver wire never restocks it. Finding 23 · Finding 07

  • Don't get talked into Zero RB. In our standard-scoring league it

    • won 9.7% of titles — barely better than autopilot. Finding 02

Rounds 4–8: quarterback and receivers

  • Take your first QB in rounds 4–6. Anywhere from 2 to 8 is fine;

    • the real mistake is waiting past round 10 and planning to stream. Finding 14 · Finding 06

  • Target the top receiver on a bad team. A team's #1 receiver

    • coming off a losing season hits top-24 43% of the time, against 25% for the rest of the mid rounds. The draft tool marks these with a green ◆. Finding 08

  • Buy targets, not efficiency. A receiver with lots of targets and

    • modest points is a buy; big points on few targets don't repeat. Finding 17

  • Touchdown luck resets. Fade last year's TD-lucky players, buy

    • the unlucky ones — the tool marks both. Finding 16

  • Skip the bounce-back-discount receiver. Top-20 two years ago,

    • cratered last year, "value" price now: that profile busts 53% of the time. Finding 09

  • Ignore "injury-prone" at QB and WR. Missed time doesn't carry

    • over at those positions — take the discount other drafters give you. Mild caution at TE only. Finding 18

  • Squint at 29–30-year-old receivers at mid-round prices. That age

    • band busted most, though the sample is thin. Finding 10

Rounds 9–12: tight end and the bench

  • Tight end in round 10 or later. Half of every year's top-8 TEs

    • cost a round-8-or-later pick or nothing at all. Finding 05

  • A second QB or TE is a free choice — the timing isn't. Take one

    • late or not at all; never early. Finding 20

  • Don't overload the bench with lottery-ticket RBs. The

    • stash-a-back theory buys about one percent of championships. Finding 19

  • Your stud RB's handcuff is insurance, not profit. Owning him

    • pays out exactly when your starter sits and adds zero edge overall — take him if he's free, never reach. Finding 13

Rounds 13–15: kicker and defense

  • Spend your last two picks here, and don't think hard. Last

    • year's kicker stats predict almost nothing. Finding 04

  • Defense: one number — the opponent's implied total. Draft

    • whoever faces the worst offenses early, then stream all season. Finding 27

  • Kicker: pick the offense and the dome, not the leg.

    • Finding 28

  • "He's on a better offense" is not a tiebreak. Vegas does know

    • which offenses will score — it just doesn't help you pick between two skill players. Finding 30

During the season

  • The waiver wire is maintenance, not strategy. Worth 5–12 points

    • a season, mostly patching QB and kicker — but a usage jump (targets, carries) is the one thing worth claiming early. Finding 22

  • Streaks mean nothing. A hot or cold last three weeks predicts

    • zero about next season — price the full season. Finding 15

  • Read injury tags like this: Out and Doubtful mean zero. When a player is Questionable, he

    • plays 69% of the time at about 83% strength. Finding 21

  • Don't overthink start/sit matchups. Opponent and weather are

    • worth about a point a week at best, and Vegas already priced them. Finding 26

Why you can trust the averages

  • **A round-1 pick returns a weekly starter 81% of the time; round 15,

    • 5%.** Early picks buy floors, late picks buy lottery tickets — spend them that way. Finding 29

  • **Losing two finals in a row is a coin-flip outcome, not a broken

    • plan.** Finding 12 · Finding 11
